checklist.step: Build and maintain the 51-jurisdiction notice/disclosure requirements matrix
actions: Open the NAIC Model #74 text and list every consumer-facing notice it drives: network disclosure in enrollment materials, provider-directory access statement, provider-termination notice, continuity-of-care notice, out-of-network/balance-billing cost disclosure and tiered-network disclosure.

For each of the 51 jurisdictions, read the state's adoption (rep: Alaska 3 AAC 26.110) on the DOI website and record on a matrix row: notice type, trigger event, timing rule, mandatory content elements, delivery channel and the statutory cite.
Save each state's source page as <state>-NA-requirements-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf into the document management repository and link it to the row.
Version the matrix and record the review date; hand the completed matrix to the Policy Forms Specialist and the Business Systems Analyst (C03) as the single source of content rules.
checklist.done: every jurisdiction has a sourced matrix row per notice type with cite, timing and content elements, and the matrix version is dated and filed.

checklist.step: Verify every matrix citation against the current state text
actions: Re-read each cited statute, regulation or bulletin as currently in force on the state legislature or DOI site, not from a secondary summary.
Confirm the matrix row's timing (e.g., 30-day pre-termination member notice) and content elements match the current text; correct and initial any drift.
Flag states whose adoption diverges materially from Model #74 (extra content elements, shorter clocks) with a VARIANT tag on the row.
Return the verified matrix to the Compliance Analyst with a dated counsel-verification note attached.
checklist.done: the matrix carries a dated counsel verification and every VARIANT state is tagged with its divergence.

checklist.step: Inventory every existing form and correspondence template that carries a network-plan notice
actions: Search the document management repository template library for enrollment kits, certificates, member handbooks, termination letters and EOB inserts used on Medical & Health network plans.
Ask the Policy Admin Ops Lead for the list of correspondence templates actually configured in the policy admin correspondence engine and reconcile it to the repository list.
Record each template on the form inventory: template id, form number and edition date, states used in, notice types it carries, current version and owner.
Mark any template found in the engine but not in the repository (or vice versa) as an orphan for immediate follow-up.
checklist.done: the form inventory lists every live template with id, edition, states and notice types, and orphans are flagged.

checklist.step: Gap-map the inventory against the requirements matrix
actions: Cross every matrix row (state × notice type) against the form inventory and mark COVERED, PARTIAL (template exists but misses a content element) or MISSING.
For PARTIAL rows, list the exact missing elements (e.g., Alaska continuity-of-care duration statement, directory-access URL and phone number).
Prioritize the gap list by member exposure: states with active network plans first, using enrollment counts pulled from the Policy Administration Platform.
Issue the gap list as build tickets to the Policy Forms Specialist in the workflow tool with due dates ahead of the next open-enrollment print deadline.
checklist.done: every state × notice cell has a coverage status and every PARTIAL/MISSING cell has an owned, dated build ticket.

checklist.step: Draft the network disclosure block for enrollment materials and certificates
actions: Draft the disclosure covering: how the network works, referral/authorization procedures, how to obtain the current provider directory (URL and toll-free number), and out-of-network cost-sharing consequences, using the matrix content elements as the checklist.
Build state-variable brackets for VARIANT states rather than separate full templates where the state allows a Statement of Variability.
Route the draft to the Content Specialist for plain-language edit without losing any mandatory element.
Store the draft as a new minor version in the document management repository with a redline against the prior edition.
checklist.done: a redlined draft disclosure exists covering every matrix content element with state variability bracketed.

checklist.step: Draft the provider-termination and continuity-of-care notice templates
actions: Draft the member termination notice with merge fields for provider name, specialty, termination effective date, alternative in-network providers and the PCP-change instructions.

Draft the continuity-of-care notice stating the transitional-care right for active courses of treatment (up to 90 days where the state so provides) and for pregnancy through postpartum care, with the application procedure and contact.

Check each VARIANT state's timing statement — the Model #74 baseline is member notice at least 30 days before the provider termination effective date or as soon as practicable — and bracket state-specific day counts.
List every merge field with its source system field name so the Configuration Engineer (C03) can map it.
checklist.done: both templates exist with bracketed state variants and a complete merge-field dictionary.

checklist.step: Draft the directory-access and out-of-network cost disclosures for point-of-service correspondence
actions: Draft the provider-directory access statement (print and online access, accuracy-reporting contact) for ID card carriers, EOBs and the Customer Self-Service Portal footer.

Draft the out-of-network disclosure stating that services from out-of-network providers may result in higher cost-sharing or balance billing, with the state-mandated wording where the matrix specifies exact text.
Confirm with the Consumer Affairs Analyst which member touchpoints the states require the disclosure on, and list each touchpoint against its template id.
File the drafts in the document management repository linked to their matrix rows.
checklist.done: directory-access and out-of-network disclosure drafts exist and each required touchpoint is mapped to a template.

checklist.step: Run readability scoring where states require it
actions: Identify from the matrix which states impose a readability standard (typically a Flesch reading ease minimum, commonly 40-50) on member notices and certificates.
Score each affected draft, record the Flesch score on the form inventory row, and rework any failing text with the Content Specialist.
Produce the readability certification page for states that require a certification to accompany a filing.
File scores and certifications with the template version in the document management repository.
checklist.done: every readability-state template has a recorded passing score and, where required, a certification page.

checklist.step: Obtain counsel review and approval of every new or changed template
actions: Review each draft against the matrix row and the underlying state text, checking mandatory elements, timing statements and any state-mandated exact wording.
Mark required changes in the redline and return to the Policy Forms Specialist; re-review until clean.
Record approval with name, date and template version on the form inventory row.
Refuse approval for any template whose matrix row lacks a current counsel-verified citation.
checklist.done: every template version carries a dated counsel approval tied to a verified citation.

checklist.step: Determine which states require the forms to be filed and file them via SERFF
actions: In SERFF open Industry ▸ Filing Rules for each affected state and the health TOI, and read whether member notices/certificate amendments require prior approval, file-and-use or no filing.
Print each state's instructions page to PDF as <state>-filing-rules-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf and file it against the determination.
For filing states, create the SERFF filing with the approved template, readability certification and cover letter, and record the SERFF Tracking Number on the form inventory row.
Track dispositions in SERFF and do not release a prior-approval state's template until Approved or the deemer period is satisfied; record the disposition date.
checklist.done: every state has a documented filing determination and filing states show a SERFF tracking number and disposition on the inventory.

checklist.step: Deploy approved templates into the correspondence engine
actions: Hand the approved template package (PDF proof, merge-field dictionary, state list, effective date) to the Configuration Engineer for load into the policy admin correspondence engine.
Verify the engine's template id, version and state routing match the form inventory row exactly.
Generate a test render for one member per state variant and compare it field-by-field to the approved proof.
Record the deployment date and engine template id on the inventory row.
checklist.done: each approved template is live in the engine with matching id, version and state routing, and a per-variant test render is on file.

checklist.step: Retire superseded template versions with clean effective dating
actions: Set the retirement date of the old version to the day before the new version's effective date in both the repository and the correspondence engine.
Confirm with the Policy Admin Ops Lead that no batch job or manual letter queue still references the retired template id.
Archive (never delete) the retired version with its approval history for the 7-year retention period.
Note the supersession chain on the form inventory row.
checklist.done: no retired template remains callable, and each inventory row shows an unbroken version chain.

checklist.step: Update the form inventory as the closing act of every change
actions: Complete the inventory row: template id, version, edition date, states, notice types, matrix rows satisfied, readability score, counsel approval date, SERFF tracking numbers, deployment date.
Attach links to the repository version, the approval note and the filing dispositions.
Have the Compliance Manager spot-check the row against the source artifacts before it is marked closed.
Export the updated inventory to the compliance evidence repository as the point-in-time record.
checklist.done: the inventory row is complete, source-linked, spot-checked and exported as evidence.

checklist.step: Wire the per-change intake trigger so future changes cannot bypass the build process
actions: Configure a mandatory 'NAIC 74 notice impact' question on the product-change and network-change intake forms in the workflow tool.
Route any YES answer automatically to the Policy Forms Specialist queue with the go-live date pre-populated and T-30/T-14/T-7 reminders armed.
Subscribe the Compliance Analyst to state DOI bulletin feeds for all 51 jurisdictions so regulatory changes also raise a matrix-update ticket.
Test the trigger with a dummy change and file the test evidence.
checklist.done: product, network and regulatory changes each demonstrably raise a routed, dated form-impact ticket.

checklist.step: Log and remediate any notice issued from a defective template
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any discovered use of an unapproved, outdated or state-mismatched template, recording affected states, notice type, member count and discovery source.
Have the Policy Forms Specialist produce the corrected template through the full build path (matrix, counsel, filing where required).
Put the re-mailing question to Regulatory Counsel — whether affected members must receive a corrected notice — and record the written decision.
Close the issue only when the corrected template is deployed and the counsel-decided remediation is complete, with sign-off dated on the issue.
checklist.done: every defective-template event has a tracker issue, a corrected deployed template and a counsel-signed remediation decision.

testing.step: Build the template population from the inventory and the engine
actions: Export the full NAIC 74 form inventory and, separately, the list of live notice templates configured in the policy admin correspondence engine.
Extract from the document management repository all template versions created or changed in the review period.
Combine into one population keyed by template id + version, covering all writing companies and 51 jurisdictions.
testing.done: a single keyed population exists combining inventory, engine and repository sources for the period.

testing.step: Reconcile inventory, repository and engine to each other
actions: Match every engine template to an inventory row and a repository version; list unmatched items in either direction.
Check version numbers and effective dates agree across all three sources.
Treat any template live in the engine with no inventory row as an automatic exception — that is an untracked notice.
testing.done: the three sources reconcile or every difference is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the method
actions: Take 100% of templates changed in the period plus a seeded random sample of 25 unchanged live templates, minimum 40 in total.
Stratify so every notice type and at least 10 jurisdictions (always including VARIANT-tagged states and Alaska as the representative state) are covered.
Record seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible, stratified sample is drawn covering all notice types and the variant states.

testing.step: Re-perform the state content check on each sampled template
actions: For each sampled template and state, read the current state text (rep: Alaska 3 AAC 26.110) directly — not the matrix — and list the mandatory content elements independently.
Compare the rendered template against that independent list element by element.
Record any missing or altered element as an exception, including 'element present but state-mandated exact wording changed'.
Capture the state source page into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled template has an independent element-by-element re-check with captured sources.

testing.step: Trace filed templates to SERFF dispositions
actions: For each sampled template in a filing state, open SERFF Filing Access and search the recorded SERFF Tracking Number.
Confirm the filed attachment is the same edition as the deployed template and the disposition (Approved/Filed) pre-dates first use.
Flag any prior-approval state where the template went live before approval or a satisfied deemer as a reportable breach.
Capture the SERFF filing detail screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: every filed sampled template traces to a matching SERFF disposition that pre-dates first use.

testing.step: Verify approvals, readability and version control on the sample
actions: Check each sampled version carries a dated Regulatory Counsel approval and, where required, a passing Flesch score and certification.
Confirm the superseded version was retired the day before the new effective date and is no longer callable in the engine.
Confirm the approval date precedes the deployment date — deploy-then-approve is an exception.
testing.done: every sampled version shows approval before deployment, required readability evidence and a clean retirement of its predecessor.

testing.step: Verify merge-field mappings render correct member data
actions: For 5 sampled templates with merge fields, generate a test render against known test-member records in the policy admin test environment.
Compare each rendered field (provider name, termination date, alternative providers, day counts) to the source record values.
Log any field pulling from the wrong source column or formatting dates against the state's stated convention as an exception.
testing.done: sampled merge fields render the correct source values for every test member.

testing.step: Test the intake trigger cannot be bypassed
actions: Pull the period's product-change and network-change records and check each shows the mandatory 'NAIC 74 notice impact' answer.
For 10 changes answered YES, trace to the routed form-impact ticket and its completion before the change's go-live date.
For 5 changes answered NO, re-judge the answer independently; a wrong NO is an exception.
testing.done: sampled changes all carry the impact answer, YES answers trace to completed tickets, and no wrong NO stands uncorrected.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with template id, states, defect and member exposure.
Assign root cause (matrix stale, counsel skipped, engine drift, intake bypass) and an owner.
Set remediation dates and mark re-mail-decision items for Regulatory Counsel.
Carry open exceptions into next year's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance content threshold and the 2% metadata tolerance.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer — who drafted or approved none of the sampled templates — sign the workpaper.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-036/C01 and report results to the Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with stated conclusion and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Intake every provider termination and material network-change event
actions: Receive the weekly provider network change feed from the network management team into the workflow tool events queue; the feed must arrive even when empty so silence is detectable.
Open each event and read: provider NPI and name, specialty, service locations, termination or change effective date, reason code and affected plan networks.
Register one event case per provider × network with a unique event id.
Chase the network management contact the same day for any feed gap or any event arriving with fewer than 45 days to its effective date.
checklist.done: every feed event is a registered case with complete data, and short-fuse events are flagged the day they arrive.

checklist.step: Validate event data before any downstream work
actions: Check the effective date is in the future and the provider exists in the provider extract used by member attribution.
Confirm the affected network ids map to live plans in the Policy Administration Platform.
Reject the event back to network management with a reason code where fields are missing or contradictory, and log the rejection on the case.
Mark validated events 'Ready for attribution'.
checklist.done: each event is either validated and marked ready or rejected with a logged reason.

checklist.step: Identify the affected covered persons for each event
actions: Run the approved attribution query in the enterprise data warehouse: members enrolled in the affected networks who have the terminating provider as PCP of record, or a claim/authorization with that provider in the trailing 12 months.
Add members with an open authorization or an active course of treatment with the provider, flagged CONTINUITY for the continuity-of-care variant notice.
Write the member list to the event case with counts by state, and reconcile the state split against plan enrollment by state for reasonableness.
Save the query text, run date and row counts to the case so the attribution is re-performable.
checklist.done: each event carries a saved, re-runnable member list with state counts and CONTINUITY flags.

checklist.step: Compute the statutory mail-by date per state on every event
actions: Look up each affected state's timing rule in the compliance matrix (baseline Model #74 §5: member notice at least 30 days before the termination effective date, or as soon as practicable when the carrier itself got less notice).
Compute mail-by date = termination effective date − the state's day count, per state on the event.
Where the carrier received under 30 days' notice from the provider, record the 'as soon as practicable' basis and set mail-by = 5 business days from event receipt.
Enter each mail-by date into the workflow SLA timer so T-10/T-5/T-2 reminders arm automatically.
checklist.done: every event shows a per-state mail-by date with its basis, and SLA timers are armed.

checklist.step: Select the correct state-approved template version for each notice
actions: In the correspondence engine, select the termination-notice template mapped to each member's state, checking the template version against the C01 form inventory's current version.
Select the continuity-of-care variant for CONTINUITY-flagged members.
Stop and raise to the Policy Forms Specialist if any state lacks a current approved template — never substitute a neighbouring state's letter.
Record template ids and versions on the event case.
checklist.done: every member row is paired to the current approved template for their state, or the event is held with a raised template gap.

checklist.step: Generate the batch and QA rendered proofs before release
actions: Generate the notice batch in proof mode and pull 2 rendered notices per state variant.

Check merge fields against source: provider name and specialty, termination effective date, alternative in-network providers within the state's time/distance standard, PCP-change instructions and the directory URL/phone.
Check the CONTINUITY variant states the transitional-care right and application procedure.
Sign the proof-check on the event case; a failed proof stops the batch and routes back to the Correspondence Clerk.
checklist.done: a signed per-variant proof check exists and no batch releases with a failed proof.

checklist.step: Scrub the mailing list for address quality and deduplication
actions: Run the member list against the returned-mail suppression history and USPS address standardization; correct addresses from the latest member record where the standardizer fails.
Deduplicate households where the state permits one notice per policy, otherwise keep per-member rows.
Route members with e-delivery consent on file to the electronic channel and the remainder to print.
Attach the scrub summary (input rows, corrected, suppressed-with-reason, channel split) to the event case.
checklist.done: the mailing list is standardized, deduplicated per state rules, channel-split, and the scrub summary is filed.

checklist.step: Release the batch to print/mail and electronic delivery
actions: Release the print stream to the mail vendor with the required in-home window and obtain the vendor's mail manifest showing piece counts and the postmark/mail date.
Trigger e-delivery for consented members via the Customer Self-Service Portal notification service and capture the send receipts.
Compare manifest + e-delivery counts to the scrubbed list count; investigate any shortfall the same day.
Confirm the actual mail date is on or before every state's mail-by date; if not, escalate immediately to the Policy Admin Ops Lead before the batch closes.
checklist.done: manifest and receipts reconcile to the list, and the mail date is on or before each mail-by date or escalated.

checklist.step: Record the delivery in the notice log
actions: Write one notice log row per event × state: event id, notice type, template id/version, member count, mail-by date, actual mail date, SLA met Y/N, manifest reference.
Attach the rendered specimen, mail manifest and e-delivery receipts to the row.
Lock the row against edit once written; corrections go on a new correction row.
checklist.done: each event × state has a locked, evidence-linked notice log row with an explicit SLA verdict.

checklist.step: Work returned mail and cure failed deliveries
actions: Log every returned piece against its notice log row within 3 business days of receipt.
Look up a better address in the Policy Administration Platform and the latest claim/billing records; re-mail within 5 business days of the return where one exists.
Where no better address exists, attempt the member's e-delivery channel or phone outreach via the Contact Center Agent and record the attempt.
Record every cure attempt and outcome on the notice log row.
checklist.done: every returned piece shows a dated cure attempt and outcome on its notice log row.

checklist.step: Intake and route continuity-of-care requests
actions: Register each continuity-of-care request (from the notice's application procedure, the contact center, or a provider) as a case linked to the triggering network event.
Verify eligibility: active course of treatment, pregnancy, or other state-defined qualifying condition, and record the qualifying basis.
Approve transitional care at in-network cost-sharing for the state's period (up to 90 days where so provided; through postpartum for pregnancy) and notify the member and provider in writing.
Record decisions and day counts so the transitional period end date is visible to claims.
checklist.done: every request has a registered case, an eligibility decision with basis, and written member/provider notification.

checklist.step: Confirm the provider directory is corrected within the update window
actions: For each event, check the online provider directory no longer lists the terminated provider as in-network within 30 days of the carrier's receipt of the change notice.
Record the directory update date on the event case and compare it to the 30-day window.
Raise a defect to the directory data owner for any listing still live past the window and track it to closure.
checklist.done: each event shows a directory update date inside the 30-day window or a tracked defect.

checklist.step: Escalate at-risk and breached deadlines immediately
actions: Act on workflow SLA escalations: at T-2 days unresolved, direct resources to release the batch; on breach, open a tracker issue the same day.
Record on the issue: event id, states, member count, days late and the cause.
Decide with Regulatory Counsel whether the breach requires a state self-report (rep: Alaska Division of Insurance) and record the written decision.
Direct the late batch to mail immediately — lateness never converts to non-delivery.
checklist.done: every breach has a same-day issue, a counsel-documented self-report decision and a completed late mailing.

checklist.step: Reconcile events to notices monthly
actions: Pull the month's provider network change feed rows and match each to a notice log row; investigate any event with no notice within 5 business days.
Review the SLA-met rate by state on the Power BI notice dashboard against the 98% threshold.
Review returned-mail cure aging and continuity-of-care case aging.
Publish the reconciliation summary to the Compliance Manager with exceptions annotated.
checklist.done: the monthly reconciliation shows every event matched or investigated, with SLA and cure metrics published.

checklist.step: File the month's notice evidence for retention
actions: Move the month's locked notice log rows, specimens, manifests, receipts and reconciliation summary into the compliance evidence repository under REG-036/C02/<yyyy-mm>.
Apply the 7-year retention label from the notice date.
Verify the repository index retrieves by event id, state and member id so DOI inquiries can be answered within 5 business days.
checklist.done: the month's evidence is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by event, state and member.

testing.step: Build the event population from the source feed, not the notice log
actions: Extract every provider-termination and material network-change row with an effective date in the quarter directly from the provider network change feed archive.
Add continuity-of-care requests received in the quarter from the case management extract.
Reconcile the feed extract count to network management's own change report for the quarter and resolve differences before sampling.
testing.done: the population is drawn from source, reconciled to the network team's records, and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile every event to a notice log row
actions: Match each population event to notice log rows on event id and state.
List any event with no notice row as an automatic 'no notice' exception — the most serious failure mode.
Check locked rows were never edited; correction rows must trace to their original.
testing.done: every event is matched or listed as a no-notice exception, and log integrity holds.

testing.step: Draw the sample
actions: Take 100% of short-fuse events (carrier received <30 days' notice) and 100% of breach-escalated events.
Add a seeded random 25 events across the remainder, stratified by state to include Alaska and at least 8 other jurisdictions.
Record seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all short-fuse and breached events plus a stratified random draw.

testing.step: Recompute the mail-by date and the SLA verdict for each sampled event
actions: Recompute mail-by = termination effective date − the state's day count from the compliance matrix, independently of the case record.
Compare the recomputed date to the recorded mail-by date and the vendor manifest's actual mail date.
Re-judge the 'as soon as practicable' basis on short-fuse events: receipt date + 5 business days.
Any SLA verdict that flips on recomputation is an exception.
testing.done: every sampled event's day-count maths is independently recomputed and verdicts reconcile or are excepted.

testing.step: Re-perform member attribution on a sub-sample
actions: For 5 sampled events, re-run the saved attribution query as of the event date in the enterprise data warehouse.
Compare the re-run member counts by state to the counts on the event case; investigate variances over 1%.
Check CONTINUITY flags caught members with open authorizations with the provider.
testing.done: re-run attribution matches the case counts within tolerance and continuity flagging is verified.

testing.step: Trace sampled notices to delivery evidence
actions: For each sampled event × state, open the notice log row and verify the rendered specimen, mail manifest and e-delivery receipts are attached and internally consistent (counts, dates).
Check the specimen used the template version that was current in the C01 inventory on the mail date.
For 10 sampled members, trace the individual to the manifest or receipt file.
testing.done: sampled notices trace end-to-end from event to member-level delivery evidence on the correct template version.

testing.step: Test returned-mail cures and directory update timing
actions: For sampled events with returns, verify each return was logged within 3 business days and cured (re-mail, e-delivery or outreach) within 5 business days of the return.
Verify the terminated provider left the online directory within 30 days of the change notice, using the recorded update date and, where available, a directory archive capture.
List cures or directory updates outside their windows as exceptions.
testing.done: sampled returns and directory updates are verified against their day-count windows.

testing.step: Test continuity-of-care decisions
actions: For 10 sampled continuity requests, re-judge eligibility against the state's qualifying conditions and the recorded clinical basis.
Check approved periods match the state rule (up to 90 days; pregnancy through postpartum) and that member and provider notifications exist.
Check denials state the reason and the appeal route.
testing.done: sampled continuity decisions are re-judged correct, correctly perioded and properly notified.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with event id, state, member exposure and days late where applicable.
Assign root cause (feed gap, attribution error, template gap, vendor delay, timer misconfigured) and an owner.
For any no-notice or >5-day-late finding, record the Head of Compliance escalation and the counsel self-report decision.
Carry open exceptions into next quarter's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, escalation where required, and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the SLA-met rate against the 98% threshold and the no-notice count against zero tolerance.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer — who released or reconciled none of the sampled batches — sign the workpaper.
File the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-036/C02 and report to the Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with computed rates, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date is on file.

checklist.step: Translate the compliance matrix into a system requirements specification
actions: Take the current counsel-verified matrix version from the Compliance Analyst (C01) and convert each state × notice-type row into a machine-enforceable rule: trigger event code, day-count formula, calendar vs business days, template id, delivery channel and hard-stop behaviour.
Record each rule in the requirements repository with a traceability link back to its matrix row and statutory cite.
Walk ambiguous rows (e.g., 'as soon as practicable') back to the Compliance Manager and record the agreed operational interpretation (receipt + 5 business days) on the requirement.
Baseline the spec version and have the Compliance Manager approve it in the repository.
checklist.done: every matrix row maps to an approved, traceable requirement with an unambiguous operational rule.

checklist.step: Design the rule-table structure
actions: Design the rule table keyed by state + notice type + trigger event, with columns for day count, day-count basis (calendar/business), direction (before/after event), template id, channel, effective-from and effective-to dates.
Design effective dating so a state rule change can be loaded ahead of its effective date without disturbing the current rule.
Design the hard-stop rules: block batch release when no rule row matches, when the mapped template version is retired in the C01 inventory, or when the computed mail-by date is already past.
Review the design with the Configuration Engineer and the Solutions Architect and file the signed design note.
checklist.done: a signed rule-table design exists with effective dating and the three hard stops specified.

checklist.step: Raise the ITSM change record before touching any environment
actions: Open a change record in ServiceNow ITSM referencing the approved spec version, the affected states and the regulatory effective date the change must beat.
Attach the implementation plan, test plan and rollback plan (restore the prior config baseline export).
Set the change tasks with due dates backed off the regulatory effective date and arm T-30/T-14/T-7 alerts.
Link the change to the C01 form-impact ticket where a template change travels with the rule change.
checklist.done: an ITSM change exists with plans attached, dated against the regulatory effective date, before any configuration work starts.

checklist.step: Configure the rule tables in the development environment
actions: Load each requirement into the policy admin system's rule table in DEV: state, notice type, trigger code, day count, basis, template id, channel, effective dates.
Configure the day-count calculator to compute mail-by dates per the rule row, honouring the calendar/business-day basis and state holidays where the basis is business days.
Configure the three hard stops from the design note.
Export the DEV rule-table content and diff it against the spec; attach the clean diff to the change record.
checklist.done: DEV configuration diffs clean against the approved spec, hard stops included.

checklist.step: Configure the event triggers from the network change feed
actions: Map the provider network change feed's event codes to the rule-table trigger codes so termination and material-change events raise notice work automatically in the workflow tool.
Configure a dead-letter queue and same-day alert to the Policy Administration Analyst for any feed row that fails mapping.
Configure the empty-feed heartbeat so a missing weekly feed raises its own alert.
Document the mapping in the requirements repository against the spec.
checklist.done: feed events raise workflow items automatically, unmappable rows alert same-day, and a missing feed self-reports.

checklist.step: Configure the SLA timers and escalation chain in the workflow tool
actions: Configure the SLA timer to arm from the computed mail-by date with T-10/T-5/T-2 business-day reminders to the Policy Administration Analyst.
Configure auto-escalation to the Policy Admin Ops Lead at T-2 and to the Compliance Officer on breach.
Verify timer arithmetic against three hand-computed examples covering calendar-day, business-day and short-fuse rules.
Attach the timer configuration screenshots to the change record.
checklist.done: timers and the escalation chain fire per the spec on all three hand-computed examples.

checklist.step: Unit test every changed rule row
actions: Build a test case per changed rule row: given an event with a known effective date, assert the computed mail-by date, the selected template id and the channel.
Add negative cases: no matching rule row, retired template version, and an event whose mail-by date is already past — each must hit its hard stop.
Run the suite in DEV and record pass/fail per case on the change record.
Return failures to the Configuration Engineer and rerun until clean.
checklist.done: every changed rule row and all three hard stops pass unit testing with recorded results.

checklist.step: Run compliance-witnessed UAT per state variant
actions: For each affected state, execute the UAT script in the UAT environment: inject a synthetic termination event, verify the mail-by date against a hand computation from the matrix, and inspect the rendered notice for the state's content elements.
Test one short-fuse event to verify the 'as soon as practicable' 5-business-day rule engages.
Sign the UAT record per state; a compliance signature is mandatory before CAB — IT cannot self-certify state rules.
Attach signed UAT records to the ITSM change.
checklist.done: every affected state has a compliance-signed UAT record including the short-fuse case.

checklist.step: Obtain CAB approval for the production deployment
actions: Present the change at CAB with the clean DEV diff, unit test results, signed UAT records and rollback plan.
Record CAB approval, the approved deployment window and the approver names on the change record.
Reject-and-reschedule rather than deploy any change missing a compliance UAT signature.
checklist.done: the change record shows CAB approval with named approvers and a scheduled window.

checklist.step: Deploy to production through the pipeline, never by hand-edit
actions: Promote the approved configuration package from UAT to production via the Azure DevOps release pipeline within the CAB window.
Record the pipeline run id and deployment timestamp on the ITSM change.
Keep the prior configuration baseline export staged for one-step rollback.
Confirm no manual production edits occurred by checking the admin audit log for the window.
checklist.done: the deployment ran through the pipeline in the window, is recorded on the change, and the audit log shows no manual edits.

checklist.step: Verify production behaviour immediately after deployment
actions: Run the production smoke pack: one synthetic event per changed state through to proof-mode rendering (no member mail), asserting mail-by date, template id and channel.
Verify the hard stops in production with a deliberately unmatched synthetic event.
Record smoke results on the change record and invoke rollback on any failure before the next real batch runs.
checklist.done: production smoke passes for every changed state and hard stop, or the change is rolled back.

checklist.step: Export and file the post-change configuration baseline
actions: Export the full production rule-table content immediately after verification, dated and hashed.
File the export in the compliance evidence repository under REG-036/C03 linked to the ITSM change id.
This baseline is the comparison point for the semi-annual divergence test and the rollback artifact for the next change.
checklist.done: a dated, hashed production baseline export is filed and linked to the change.

checklist.step: Restrict rule-table edit access to the change process
actions: Constrain production rule-table write access to the deployment pipeline service account; human accounts get read-only.
Certify the access list quarterly through the IAM platform's access review, with the Business Systems Analyst as certifier.
Alert on any direct production write by a human account via the admin audit log feed to the SIEM.
File the quarterly certification in the evidence repository.
checklist.done: only the pipeline account can write production rules, access is certified quarterly, and human writes alert.

checklist.step: Close the change with regulatory-date confirmation
actions: Confirm the deployment date beat the regulatory effective date recorded on the change; if it did not, open a tracker issue for the exposure window before closing.
Complete the change record with all artifacts attached: spec, diffs, tests, UAT, CAB, pipeline id, smoke, baseline export.
Notify the Compliance Manager and the Policy Admin Ops Lead that the rules are live.
checklist.done: the change closed complete with the regulatory date beaten or the exposure window logged as an issue.

checklist.step: Maintain the regression pack for future rule changes
actions: Add this change's unit and UAT cases to the standing NAIC 74 regression pack so future changes re-prove old states.
Tag each case with its state and matrix row for selective runs.
Run the full pack at least semi-annually and before any multi-state change, filing results in the evidence repository.
checklist.done: the regression pack includes the new cases and a full run is scheduled and filed semi-annually.

testing.step: Build the population of configuration changes and the deployed rule set
actions: Extract from ServiceNow ITSM every change record touching NAIC 74 rule tables, correspondence config or SLA timers in the half-year.
Extract the production admin audit log for the same period to capture any configuration write outside those changes.
Export the current production rule-table content as the as-deployed set.
testing.done: the population covers all recorded changes, all audit-log writes and the full as-deployed rule set.

testing.step: Reconcile audit-log writes to approved changes
actions: Match every production configuration write in the audit log to a CAB-approved ITSM change and its pipeline run id.
Treat any write with no matching change — especially by a human account — as an automatic unauthorized-change exception.
Check the pipeline service account is the only writer, per the IAM design.
testing.done: every production write maps to an approved change or is excepted as unauthorized.

testing.step: Diff the full production rule set against the counsel-verified matrix
actions: Load the as-deployed rule-table export and the current matrix side by side and compare every state × notice-type row: day count, basis, direction, template id, channel, effective dates.
List every divergence with its live period computed from the effective dates and baseline history.
For each divergence, quantify the notice impact by querying how many notices the wrong rule generated (hand to the Data Analyst).
testing.done: a complete rule-to-matrix diff exists with live periods and notice impact quantified for every divergence.

testing.step: Sample changes and verify the control sequence on each
actions: Take 100% of emergency/expedited changes plus a seeded random 15 of the remainder.
For each, verify the sequence held: approved spec → clean DEV diff → unit tests → compliance-signed UAT per state → CAB approval → pipeline deployment → production smoke → baseline export.
Any missing compliance UAT signature or post-deploy approval is an exception regardless of outcome.
testing.done: every sampled change shows the full control sequence in order, or the gap is excepted.

testing.step: Re-perform the day-count computation for sampled rules
actions: For 10 sampled state rules, hand-compute the mail-by date for a synthetic event (including one business-day-basis state with a holiday in the window and one short-fuse case).
Run the same events through the UAT environment's calculator and compare.
Any arithmetic difference is an exception with the affected state's live notices flagged for impact review.
testing.done: hand computations match the system calculator for all sampled rules including holiday and short-fuse cases.

testing.step: Verify the hard stops actually block in production-equivalent conditions
actions: In UAT (production-config mirror), inject an event with no matching rule row, one mapped to a retired template version, and one with a past mail-by date.
Confirm each is blocked with the correct hold reason and alert, and nothing renders or queues for mail.
File the blocked-event evidence in the workpaper.
testing.done: all three hard stops demonstrably block with correct reasons in production-equivalent config.

testing.step: Verify trigger coverage from the feed
actions: Sample 15 feed events from the period and confirm each raised a workflow item automatically with the right trigger code.
Check the dead-letter queue for the period and confirm every unmappable row alerted and was resolved.
Confirm the empty-feed heartbeat fired for any week without a feed.
testing.done: sampled events auto-raised work, dead letters were alerted and resolved, and heartbeat gaps fired.

testing.step: Review access and segregation of duties
actions: Pull the production rule-table access list from the IAM platform and confirm write access is limited to the pipeline service account.
Verify the quarterly access certifications were completed on time by the Business Systems Analyst.
Confirm no individual both authored a spec and approved its CAB record in the sampled changes.
testing.done: access is pipeline-only, certifications are current, and no sampled change was self-approved.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with the affected states, live period and quantified notice impact.
Assign root cause (spec error, config drift, skipped UAT, unauthorized write) and an owner.
For divergences that produced mistimed or wrong-content notices, route the member-impact assessment to the Compliance Officer under C02's cure process.
Carry open exceptions into the next semi-annual test.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, member-impact routing where needed, and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute results against the zero-divergence and zero-unauthorized-change thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Sign as independent reviewer, having specified, configured or approved none of the sampled changes.
File the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-036/C03 and report to the Compliance Committee and the Head of IT.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to both governance owners.

checklist.step: Derive the required-trainee roster from HRIS role assignments
actions: Run the HRIS report of all active employees and contractors in the in-scope job profiles: policy administration notice staff, correspondence clerks, contact center agents on health lines, complaints staff, policy forms specialists and nurse case managers.
Confirm the in-scope job-profile list with each department head (Policy Admin Ops Lead, Contact Center Ops Manager, Complaints Manager) in writing and file the confirmations.
Include contractors and vendor staff performing in-scope work, sourced from the Vendor Manager's active engagement list.
Freeze the roster with a run date and hand it to the Learning & Development Specialist for assignment.
checklist.done: a dated roster exists covering employees and contractors, with written department-head confirmations of the in-scope profiles.

checklist.step: Refresh the curriculum from the current compliance matrix
actions: Take the current counsel-verified matrix version from the Compliance Analyst and update the course modules: what NAIC 74 requires, the notice types and their triggers, state timing variations, continuity-of-care rights, directory accuracy duties and complaint signals to watch for.

Update the role-specific scenario exercises — e.g., a correspondence clerk computing a mail-by date; a contact center agent handling a 'my doctor left the network' call; a case manager judging continuity eligibility.
Record on the curriculum version page which matrix version it teaches and what changed from last year.
Route the draft to the Compliance Manager for substance review.
checklist.done: the curriculum is updated, version-linked to the matrix, and its year-over-year changes are documented.

checklist.step: Obtain SME and counsel review of the refreshed content
actions: Review the legal statements in every module against the matrix and the underlying state texts, correcting any overstatement or omission (rep check: the Alaska 3 AAC 26.110 material).
Have the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager review the complaint-handling module against actual DOI complaint patterns from C05.
Record both reviews with names and dates on the curriculum version page.
Block release of any module lacking both sign-offs.
checklist.done: every module carries dated counsel and market-conduct sign-offs on the version page.

checklist.step: Build the assessment with a defensible pass bar
actions: Write a question bank of at least 30 items mapped to the modules, including scenario questions requiring an actual day-count computation and a content-element identification.
Configure the assessment to draw 15 random questions per attempt with an 80% pass mark and a mandatory retake after failure, with the second failure routing to manager-led remediation.
Pilot the assessment with 5 experienced staff nominated by the Policy Admin Ops Lead and fix ambiguous items.
File the question bank and pilot results with the curriculum version.
checklist.done: a piloted 30-item bank exists with 15-question randomized draws, an 80% pass mark and a two-failure remediation path.

checklist.step: Load the course and assessment into the LMS
actions: Create the new curriculum version in Cornerstone LMS as a distinct course version so prior-year completions stay attributed to the prior version.
Attach the assessment with the configured pass mark and retake rules.
Run a test enrollment end-to-end (launch, complete, pass, certificate) with a test account and file the evidence.
Retire last year's version from new assignment while preserving its records.
checklist.done: the new version is live in the LMS, end-to-end tested, and the old version is closed to new assignment with records intact.

checklist.step: Assign the annual training with due dates and reminders
actions: Assign the course to every roster member by March 1 with an April 30 due date.
Configure LMS reminders at assignment, T-14, T-7 and T-1, and overdue notices to the trainee's manager.
Reconcile the LMS assignment count to the frozen roster count and resolve every difference by name before the cycle opens.
Notify department heads of their teams' due dates.
checklist.done: assignments match the roster name-for-name, reminders are armed, and the cycle opened by March 1.

checklist.step: Wire the new-hire and role-change trigger
actions: Configure the HRIS-to-LMS feed so hire or transfer into an in-scope job profile auto-assigns the course with a due date 30 days from the start/transfer date.
Test the trigger with one new-hire record and one transfer record and file the evidence.
Set a weekly exception report of in-scope starters with no assignment, routed to the Learning & Development Specialist.
checklist.done: in-scope starters and transfers are auto-assigned with 30-day due dates, and gaps surface on a weekly report.

checklist.step: Monitor completion weekly and chase non-completers
actions: Pull the weekly completion dashboard by department and send the overdue list to each department head and the Compliance Manager.
Contact each trainee overdue by more than 7 days directly and record the contact.
Track completion percentage against the April 30 deadline trajectory and flag departments trending below plan at T-14.
checklist.done: weekly overdue lists go to managers, individual chases are recorded, and at-risk departments are flagged before the deadline.

checklist.step: Enforce consequences for non-completion
actions: On May 1, log every non-completer as a tracker exception with role, department and days overdue.
Agree the enforcement action with the department head and HR Business Partner — typically removal from notice-processing or member-facing queues until complete.
Record the enforcement action and its start date on the exception.
Report the non-completer list and actions to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: every non-completer has a logged exception with an active, dated enforcement action.

checklist.step: Route assessment failures through remediation
actions: Review each second-failure case and deliver a targeted coaching session on the failed topic areas, using the item-level results from the LMS.
Have the trainee re-attempt within 10 business days of coaching.
Record the coaching date, topics and final outcome in the LMS record.
Escalate anyone failing after coaching to the Compliance Manager for a role-suitability discussion with the manager.
checklist.done: every second failure shows a coached retake within 10 business days and a recorded final outcome or escalation.

checklist.step: Trigger off-cycle refresher on material regulatory change
actions: When the C01 matrix changes materially (new state adoption, changed day count, new notice type), assess within 10 business days whether a targeted refresher is needed and record the assessment.
Where needed, have the Instructional Designer produce a short delta module and assign it to affected roles within 60 days of the rule change.
Track the delta module completion under the same chase-and-enforce mechanics as the annual cycle.
checklist.done: every material matrix change has a dated refresher assessment and, where triggered, a delta module assigned within 60 days.

checklist.step: Cover contractors and vendor staff
actions: For vendor staff performing in-scope work (e.g., mail-house exception handling, outsourced contact center), obtain either LMS completion or the vendor's equivalent training evidence mapped to the curriculum topics.
Review the vendor's training evidence against the curriculum topic list and record the mapping.
Log any vendor unable to evidence equivalent training as an exception and restrict their staff from in-scope work until cured.
checklist.done: every in-scope vendor shows completion or mapped-equivalent evidence, and unevidenced vendors are restricted.

checklist.step: Report cycle results to governance
actions: Compile the cycle report: completion rate by department, assessment pass rates, first-time-pass rate, non-completer dispositions and vendor coverage.
Compare against last year's results and note curriculum areas with weak item-level scores for next year's refresh.
Present to the Compliance Committee and file the deck and minutes reference.
checklist.done: a year-over-year cycle report is presented to the Compliance Committee and filed.

checklist.step: Close the cycle with Head of Compliance sign-off
actions: Review the cycle report, the exception log and every non-completer's disposition.
Sign the cycle closure memo confirming the training obligation is met for the year or stating the residual exceptions and their enforcement state.
Date the sign-off and file it with the cycle records.
checklist.done: a dated closure memo signed by the Head of Compliance covers completion, exceptions and enforcement.

checklist.step: Retain the training records for the retention period
actions: Archive the frozen roster, curriculum version with sign-offs, question bank, completion and score extracts, exception log and closure memo into the compliance evidence repository under REG-036/C04/<year>.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
Verify retrieval by employee id and by year so an examiner request can be met within 5 business days.
checklist.done: the full cycle record is archived, retention-labelled and retrievable by employee and year.

testing.step: Independently derive the required-trainee population from HRIS
actions: Re-run the in-scope job-profile query in HRIS for the training year, including anyone who held an in-scope role for any part of the year and contractors from the vendor engagement list.
Do not start from the LMS assignment list — the point is to catch people never assigned.
Compare the derived population to the frozen roster and list every person in one but not the other.
testing.done: an independently derived population exists and every roster difference is listed.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to LMS assignments and completions
actions: Match every population member to an LMS assignment of the correct curriculum version.
Extract completion status, completion date and best assessment score for each.
Treat any in-scope person with no assignment as an automatic roster-gap fail.
testing.done: every population member maps to an assignment with extracted status and score, or is failed as a roster gap.

testing.step: Draw the sample
actions: Take 100% of non-completers, second-failures and vendor-equivalence cases.
Add a seeded random 25 completers stratified across departments and including at least 5 new hires and 2 transfers.
Record seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all adverse cases plus a stratified completer draw.

testing.step: Verify completion evidence and scores for the sample
actions: Open each sampled LMS record and verify completion date on or before the due date, a passing score ≥80%, and attribution to the current curriculum version — not last year's.
For retakes, verify the coaching record precedes the passing attempt.
Capture record screenshots into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled record shows timely completion, a passing score on the current version, and coached retakes where applicable.

testing.step: Recompute the new-hire 30-day timing
actions: For sampled new hires and transfers, compute start/transfer date + 30 days from HRIS and compare to the LMS due date and actual completion date.
List any auto-assignment that fired late or not at all as a trigger failure, separate from individual lateness.
Check the weekly no-assignment exception report actually ran during the sampled weeks.
testing.done: new-hire timing is recomputed from HRIS dates and trigger failures are separated from trainee lateness.

testing.step: Verify curriculum currency and sign-offs
actions: Confirm the delivered curriculum version cites the matrix version that was current at assignment, and spot-check 3 modules against the matrix content (including the Alaska representative material).
Verify dated counsel and market-conduct sign-offs exist on the version page.
Verify any material matrix change in the year has its refresher assessment and, where triggered, a delta module assigned within 60 days.
testing.done: the taught content matches the then-current matrix with both sign-offs, and off-cycle triggers were honoured.

testing.step: Test enforcement actions for non-completers
actions: For every non-completer, verify a tracker exception exists with a dated enforcement action agreed with the department head.
Where the action was queue removal, verify against workflow tool queue assignments that the person was actually removed until completion.
An enforcement action recorded but not executed is an exception in its own right.
testing.done: every non-completer's enforcement action is verified as actually executed, not merely recorded.

testing.step: Test vendor-equivalence evidence
actions: For each sampled vendor case, review the vendor's training evidence and the recorded topic mapping against the curriculum topic list.
Judge independently whether the evidence genuinely covers the NAIC 74 topics or is a generic compliance course.
Verify restricted vendors were actually kept off in-scope work during the restriction.
testing.done: vendor evidence is independently judged topic-adequate and restrictions are verified as enforced.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception: roster gaps, late triggers, unexecuted enforcement, stale content, vendor shortfalls.
Assign root cause (HRIS profile mapping, feed failure, manager non-enforcement) and an owner.
Set remediation dates; roster-gap individuals get immediate assignment with a 15-business-day due date.
Carry open exceptions into next year's test.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and date, and roster-gap individuals are immediately assigned.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the completion-with-pass rate against the 100%-or-enforced threshold and count roster-gap fails.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Sign as independent reviewer, having neither administered assignments nor authored curriculum.
File the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-036/C04 and report to the Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with computed rates and a stated conclusion is filed and reported.

checklist.step: Stand up and maintain the network-adequacy complaint taxonomy
actions: Define the tag set in the case tool: ACCESS-NO-PROVIDER, ACCESS-WAIT-TIME, ACCESS-DISTANCE, DIRECTORY-INACCURATE, BALANCE-BILL, NOTICE-MISSED, CONTINUITY-DENIED.
Write a one-page tagging guide with two worked examples per tag and publish it to the Complaints team and contact center knowledge base.
Map each tag to the MCAS complaint reason codes so year-end reconciliation is mechanical.
Review the taxonomy annually against the past year's 'other' bucket and split any tag exceeding 20% of volume.
checklist.done: the tag set, tagging guide and MCAS mapping are published and annually reviewed.

checklist.step: Capture complaints from every intake channel
actions: Register every written complaint, portal submission and escalated call as a case within 1 business day of receipt, with the received date preserved as the member's contact date — not the registration date.
Configure Genesys call dispositions so agents flag network-access grievances at the point of call for next-day case creation.

Check each state DOI portal (rep: Alaska Division of Insurance consumer services) on its notification cadence and register DOI-forwarded complaints the day they appear, capturing the state's stated response deadline onto the case.
Apply the taxonomy tag and the member's state at registration.
checklist.done: all channels feed registered, dated, tagged cases and DOI complaints carry their state deadline from day one.

checklist.step: Acknowledge the complainant within 2 business days
actions: Send the acknowledgment using the approved template (a C01 inventory template), naming the handler and the expected response window.
Record the acknowledgment date on the case; the SLA field computes business days from receipt automatically.
For DOI-forwarded complaints, acknowledge to the DOI in the form the state specifies.
checklist.done: every case shows an acknowledgment within 2 business days to the member and, where applicable, the DOI.

checklist.step: Investigate access complaints by re-verifying the network position
actions: For ACCESS and DISTANCE tags, re-run the time/distance check for the member's home address against in-network providers of the needed specialty in the enterprise data warehouse, and record whether the state's standard is actually met.
For WAIT-TIME tags, call three listed in-network providers of the specialty and record the first-available appointment offered against the state's wait-time standard.
For DIRECTORY-INACCURATE tags, verify the disputed listing against the provider contract status and log a directory defect where the member is right.
Write the factual finding — standard met or not met — on the case before any resolution is drafted.
checklist.done: every access complaint carries a recorded re-verification with a met/not-met finding against the state standard.

checklist.step: Resolve the member's individual problem
actions: Where the standard is not met, arrange the concrete fix: an in-network appointment within the standard, an out-of-network authorization at in-network cost-sharing, or a continuity-of-care approval via the Medical / Nurse Case Manager.
For BALANCE-BILL tags, engage the Claims Analyst to reprocess at in-network cost-sharing where the directory or notice failure caused the exposure.
Send the resolution letter from the approved template stating what was done and the member's further appeal rights.
Record the resolution category and date on the case.
checklist.done: each complaint shows a concrete member remedy, a resolution letter and a recorded category and date.

checklist.step: Respond to the DOI inside the state deadline
actions: Draft the DOI response with the timeline of events, the re-verification finding, the member remedy and the corrective steps, in the state's required format.
Compute the due date from the DOI letter and the matrix (commonly 15-21 calendar days) and submit through the state's channel with proof of submission captured.
Route any response conceding a network deficiency or systemic failure through Regulatory Counsel before submission.
Record the submitted date and attach the response and proof to the case.
checklist.done: every DOI complaint shows a submitted, evidenced response inside the state deadline, counsel-cleared where conceding.

checklist.step: Run the weekly mis-tag and aging review
actions: Review a sample of 10 newly closed cases weekly for tag accuracy against the tagging guide and correct mis-tags on the case with a correction note.
Review the aging report for cases approaching acknowledgment or DOI deadlines and reassign workload where a handler is backing up.
Feed recurring tagging errors back to the Trainer for the next C04 coaching cycle.
checklist.done: weekly tag-accuracy and aging reviews are recorded with corrections and workload actions.

checklist.step: Sweep untagged complaints and calls for missed network-adequacy grievances
actions: Run the monthly keyword query (network, directory, 'no doctor', 'can't find', wait time, balance bill, out-of-network) across untagged complaint text and Genesys call disposition notes.
Deliver hits to the Complaints Manager, who judges each and retro-tags genuine network-adequacy cases.
Track the monthly miss rate; a rate over 5% triggers a tagging-guide refresh and targeted coaching.
checklist.done: the monthly sweep runs, hits are adjudicated and retro-tagged, and the miss rate is tracked against 5%.

checklist.step: Trend the complaint data monthly
actions: Refresh the Power BI complaint dashboard: volume by tag, state, plan network and provider specialty, with 12-month trend lines.
Compute the complaint rate per 1,000 members by state so small states' spikes are visible.
Flag any tag × state cell whose volume doubles month-over-month or exceeds its 12-month mean by 2 standard deviations.
Publish the monthly trend note to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager and the Compliance Committee pack.
checklist.done: the dashboard is refreshed with rates and flags, and the monthly trend note is published.

checklist.step: Run root-cause analysis on every cluster
actions: For every flagged cluster and any ≥3 complaints sharing a tag + state + specialty, read the underlying cases and name the root cause: network gap, stale directory data, notice batch failure, misconfigured rule, or member communication defect.
Record the root cause with the supporting case ids on a root-cause record in the case tool.
Distinguish one-off handling errors from systemic causes — only systemic causes proceed to remediation routing.
checklist.done: every cluster has a named, case-linked root cause classified one-off or systemic.

checklist.step: Route remediation to the owning control and track to closure
actions: Open a tracker issue per systemic root cause and assign it to the owning control: template defects to the Policy Forms Specialist (C01), notice failures to the Policy Admin Ops Lead (C02), rule misconfigurations to the Business Systems Analyst (C03), directory data to the Data Quality Analyst, and genuine network gaps to the provider network team with the access-plan owner informed.
Set a remediation date proportionate to member impact and verify implementation evidence before closure.
Sign off closure personally and link the closed issue back to the root-cause record.
Where a genuine network gap is confirmed, notify the Regulatory Filing Specialist so the state access-plan filing (rep: Alaska Division of Insurance) reflects the gap and its cure plan.
checklist.done: every systemic root cause has an owned, dated, evidence-verified and signed-off remediation, with access-plan impacts routed.

checklist.step: Escalate serious patterns to governance
actions: Review monthly any state showing repeated DOI complaints on the same tag, any missed-DOI-deadline event and any confirmed uncured network gap.
Decide whether proactive DOI engagement is warranted before the state escalates to a market conduct exam, with Regulatory Counsel advising.
Record decisions and rationale in the Compliance Committee minutes.
checklist.done: serious patterns receive a recorded governance decision on proactive regulator engagement.

checklist.step: Reconcile complaint counts to MCAS at year-end
actions: Extract the year's complaint register by state and MCAS reason-code mapping and reconcile to the counts reported in the MCAS filing.
Investigate and document any difference before the MCAS submission deadline.
File the reconciliation with the MCAS workpapers.
checklist.done: register counts reconcile to MCAS by state and reason code with documented differences resolved.

checklist.step: Keep complaint files exam-ready
actions: On closure, verify each file holds the intake record, acknowledgment, investigation and re-verification notes, resolution letter and DOI correspondence, then archive to the compliance evidence repository under REG-036/C05.
Apply the 7-year retention label from the closure date.
Verify retrieval by case id, member id and state within the 5-business-day exam standard.
checklist.done: closed files are complete, archived, retention-labelled and retrievable within the exam standard.

checklist.step: Review the monitoring program itself annually
actions: Assess annually whether the taxonomy, keyword sweep, thresholds and dashboards still catch what the DOIs are seeing — compare against the states' published complaint indices where available.
Adjust thresholds and keywords from the year's miss-rate and cluster history.
Record the annual review and its changes in the procedure document with Head of Compliance approval.
checklist.done: an annual program review is recorded with approved threshold and taxonomy adjustments.

testing.step: Build the complaint population including the untagged sweep
actions: Extract all complaints closed in the quarter with network-adequacy tags from the case tool.
Independently re-run the keyword sweep over all untagged complaints and Genesys dispositions for the quarter — do not reuse the Data Analyst's runs.
Combine tagged cases and adjudicated sweep hits into the test population.
testing.done: the population includes tagged cases plus an independently swept untagged set.

testing.step: Reconcile DOI-forwarded complaints to the state portals
actions: For 5 states including Alaska, compare the DOI complaints registered in the case tool against the state portal's list for the quarter.
List any DOI complaint present on a portal but absent from the case tool as an automatic intake-failure exception.
Verify captured response deadlines match the DOI letters.
testing.done: portal-to-register reconciliation is complete for the sampled states with intake failures excepted.

testing.step: Draw the sample
actions: Take 100% of DOI-forwarded complaints and 100% of sweep hits judged network-adequacy.
Add a seeded random 25 member-direct complaints stratified by tag and state.
Record seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all DOI cases and sweep hits plus a stratified member draw.

testing.step: Re-judge the tag on every sampled case
actions: Read each sampled complaint's own words and independently assign a tag from the tagging guide before looking at the recorded tag.
Compare and compute the mis-tag rate against the 5% threshold.
Note systematically confused tag pairs for the taxonomy's annual review.
testing.done: every sampled case has an independent tag judgement and the mis-tag rate is computed.

testing.step: Recompute acknowledgment and DOI response timeliness
actions: Recompute business days from the preserved receipt date to the acknowledgment date for every sampled case against the 2-business-day standard.
Recompute the DOI due date from the DOI letter and the state's matrix deadline, and compare to the evidenced submission date.
Verify the received date was not overwritten by the registration date — sample the original letters/emails for 5 cases.
testing.done: timeliness is recomputed from source dates and any SLA verdict that flips is an exception.

testing.step: Re-perform the access re-verification on a sub-sample
actions: For 5 sampled ACCESS/DISTANCE cases, re-run the time/distance check with the member's address and specialty as of the complaint date.
Compare the re-run met/not-met finding to the recorded finding; a flipped finding is an exception with the resolution re-opened.
Check WAIT-TIME cases documented three provider contacts with offered appointment dates.
testing.done: re-run verifications match the recorded findings or the case is excepted and reopened.

testing.step: Verify member remedies and DOI response content
actions: For sampled not-met cases, verify the concrete remedy occurred: the authorization exists in the system, the appointment was arranged, or the claim was reprocessed at in-network cost-sharing.
Read sampled DOI responses for factual consistency with the case file and confirm counsel clearance where a deficiency was conceded.
Check resolution letters used current C01 inventory templates.
testing.done: sampled remedies are verified in-system and DOI responses are consistent, cleared and on approved templates.

testing.step: Test cluster detection and remediation follow-through
actions: Independently recompute the quarter's clusters (≥3 same tag + state + specialty) from the population and compare to the root-cause records raised.
For each systemic root cause, verify the tracker issue reached the correct owning control and closure carries implementation evidence and the Market Conduct sign-off.
Verify confirmed network gaps were notified to the access-plan filing owner.
An undetected cluster or an evidence-free closure is an exception.
testing.done: independently computed clusters all trace to owned, evidenced, signed-off remediations including access-plan routing.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per test exception with case id, state and category.
Assign root cause (intake miss, date overwrite, deadline mis-set, re-verification skipped, cluster missed) and an owner.
Reopen member cases where the remedy was not actually delivered.
Carry open exceptions into next quarter's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and date, with undelivered remedies reopened.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute results against the thresholds: 100% DOI timeliness, ≥95% acknowledgment, ≤5% mis-tag, all clusters remediated.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Sign as independent reviewer, having handled, supervised or trended none of the sampled complaints.
File the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-036/C05 and report to the Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with threshold results and a stated conclusion is filed and reported.
